text: SEAMEN JAILED.

label: text
text: REVOLVER

label: text
text: A CAPTAIN'S STORY.

label: text
text: Unruly Indians Who Had to Be Locked Up.

label: text
text:
Order was only restored on board the S.S. "City of Corinth," when a few days from Hongkong, by the captain procuring revolvers to protect the loyal part of his crew against "picketing" by nine firemen who gave trouble as far back as June, when they adopted "a ca" eanny policy because they were tired.
These nine Indian firemen were tried and sentenced at the Marine Court this morning.
On the first charge of disobedience to the lawful commands of the master at Manila on August

label: text
text: After the master had given evidence, the Magistrate (L.T. (Com. G. F. Holt, R.N.), added a second charge of combining to impede the navigation of the ship; on this defendants each received an additional twelve weeks.

label: paragraph_title
text: Pay to be "Docked."

label: text
text:
Both sentences were, with hard labour," to run consecutively (meaning sixteen weeks in all), without the option of a fine.
His Worship also ordered that "any wages that may be due, to be used for their subsistence while undergoing their sentence and the residue for their repatriation to Bombay."

label: text
text: Mr. L. R. Andrewes appeared for the prosecution.

label: text
text: tain G. J. D. Burton, who explained that defendants were all members of his crew, on articles which had not yet expired. They began to give trouble in the North Atlantic, when off Gibraltar, saying that they were tired and that there was no need to maintain speed as they were carrying neither mail nor passengers.

label: paragraph_title
text: Previous Trouble

label: text
text: Things continued till Manila where the men were refused shore leave because of the strict laws there regarding deserters from ships.

label: text
text: Trouble broke out, the men openly refused to work even when summoned before the captain. The British Consul-General went on board and explained the penalties to defendants. The Consul informed witness that the civil authorities in Manila could give no assistance and suggested that the men should be brought to Hongkong to be dealt with here. Subsequently the defendants, said Captain Burton, picketed the storehold door, "driving on deck the men who were working and refusing to allow any one to go below."

label: paragraph_title
text: Pút in Irons.

label: text
text: "To safeguard the loyal men,' remarked Captain Burton, 'I procured revolvers."

label: text
text: Explaining that the loyal men were so intimidated, that they dared not work, witness added that defendants were put in irons. They were removed to the House of Detention and then brought to Hongkong.

label: text
text: Confirmatory evidence was given by Mr. W. Kirk (chief engineer) and Mr. T. McKinney (second engineer).

label: text
text:
Defendants declined to cross-
examine but one of them made a
statement.

label: text
text: His Worship found all the men guilty on both charges and imposed sentence as stated.

label: text
text: The report of captain states that the crew consists of 18 British and 42 Asiatics.

label: paragraph_title
text: MAGISTRACY ITEMS.

label: text
text: EXHIBITS IN COURT.

label: text
text: More than the usual number of assault cases and lareniess made up the charge sheets at the Central Magistracy this morning before Mr. R. E. Lindsell.

label: text
text:
A blacksmith, from Shaukiwan with a wounded head was the complainant in an assault charge against a boat builder, the wound stated to have been inflicted with a wooden pole when complainant went on Saturday morning to collect the balance of an old debt amounting to $1.55. Complaintant alleged that he was attacked by the defendant and three others.
Defendant was fined $3 and ordered to sign a personal bond for future good behaviour. He was further ordered to pay $2 as compensation to the complainant, thus satisfying the debt.

label: text
text: Two scavenging coolies were involved in another case, the aggrieved party appearing with a wounded leg. An iron bar was brought to prove the assault.

label: text
text: Complainant said that they had a dispute yesterday over a broom and he was attacked at Leighton Hill Road this morning.

label: text
text: Defendant attempted to prove that he was also assaulted, but he had to pay a fine of $5, or go to prison for seven days.

label: text
text: Sergeant James. of the Aberdeen Police Station, charged two women and a man with assaulting another women who was in hospital with a deep wound in the thigh.

label: text
text: The injured woman was unable to say how she received the wound, and Sergeant James thought it possible that she fell over an anchor which was found there, as alleged by the defendants in their statements to the police and in court.

label: text
text: Defendants were remanded to bail for one week.

label: text
text: In explanation of a charge of unlawful possession of a bundle of copper wire and metal, a Chinese boy told the Magistrate that he found them in a lane at Wanchai.

label: text
text: Div.-Inspector Blackman said that inquiries had been made since Saturday morning to trace the owner, but without success. The boy received eight strokes with a light cane.

label: text
text:
An apprentice-failed to get away with a bucket containing ten pounds of tin soldier, the property of the Taikoo Docks. He was charged with theft.
Defendant, who pleaded that he was pressed to commit the theft owing to starvation, was sentenced to four weeks' hard labour.

label: paragraph_title
text: STREET FIGHTS.

label: text
text:
CANTON CURBING MOB
ROWDIES?

label: text
text: LABOURERS' DISPUTES.

label: text
text: Continual riots and fights between opposing bodies of workmen in Canton have led to about fifteen being arrested by the Department of Public Safety (Police Commissioner) on Saturday night.

label: text
text: The, trouble has spread to several Unions and the real_casus belli has now been lost sight of:

label: text
text: In different parts of the city rowdies have met and fought, causing considerable unrest. Most of the men were armed with all kinds of weapons.

label: text
text: The authorities have taken action and it is believed that the trouble is in hand. Armed police patrols were out again on Saturday, it is reported.

label: text
text: On the Taiping maloo, leading into the western suburb from the Bund, seventeen men are stated to have been killed or seriously wounded on Friday.

label: text
text: The postal strikers are expected to return to work today.

label: text
text: A correspondent to the "Wan Tsz Yat Po" states that the tea-house and (wheat) flour workers were mainly concerned; and that the strike of oilshop employees has been settled.

label: text
text: The s.s. "Szechuen" reports the suspected suicide of a second-class Chinese passenger from Shanghai. She left that port on August 8 and he man was posted missing the second day out.

label: paragraph_title
text: ARMS IN BOOTS.

label: text
text: PIRACY PREVENTED?

label: text
text: Five Chinese passengers of the s.s. "Suiyang" who trited to put into practice a stratagem one sometimes sees recorded in a cinema plot, were all arrested and charged this morning before Mr.

label: text
text:
H. B. Ninh at the Kowloon
lagistracy with unlawful possession of arms.

label: text
text:
While Detective Sergeant Barnicle of the Water Police was searching the luggage of various passengers of the "Suiyang," which sailed yesterday for Shanghai, he found in the accuseds' luggage' three pairs of brown boots, each containing a fully loaded revolver. The revolvers were hidden between the soles of the shoes, and so carefully finished was the handiwork, that nothing unusual would be noticed even by a keen observer. It was only when handling and noticing the unusual weight that Detective Barnicle discovered the arms.
When the charge was gead to the defendants this morning, one of them pleaded "Guilty" and assumed all the responsibility. The other defendants pleaded "Not Guilty" and denied having had any participation in the affair.
It is thought that the arms were going to be used for an intended piracy in Shanghai.

label: text
text: The case was remanded until Friday.

label: paragraph_title
text: SHOT & ROBBED.

label: text
text: FOREIGNER HELD UP IN SHANGHAI.

label: text
text: NO WARNING GIVEN.

label: text
text: A foreigner named J. W. Elliott, Clerk of Works of the P.W.D., was driving along Keswick Road yesterday evening when five robbers stopped the car, wounded Mr. Elliott, and robbed him of $60.

label: text
text: It is reported that Mr. Elliott was not ordered to stop, but that the shot was fired without warning.

label: text
text: It pierced his left arm and slightly injured him in the chest.

label: text
text: Mr. Elliott, was taken to hospital.

label: text
text: None of the gang has been arrested.—Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text: MIDNIGHT BLAZE.

label: text
text: YAUMATI MEDICINE SHOP DESTROYED.

label: text
text: BRIGADE SAVES BUILDING.

label: text
text: A fire broke out in Kowloon a few minutes before midnight, last night, in the ground floor of a three-storied building, the second block in Shanghai Street near the junction of Public Square Street, Yaumati.

label: text
text: Two appliances left the Kowloon Fire Station, followed by one from the Mongkok Station on the "home call" being given. Three deliveries tackled the fire from different angles, one of them being brought in from a lane at the rear of the building.

label: text
text: The efforts of the Brigade confined the fire to the ground floor, used as a herbalists' shop, where the stock of medicine leaves was destroyed. The fire spread to the ceiling and affected part of the first floor planking, but this was checked by the firemen taking a hose to the floor by ladder. The contents of this portion of the building used as a dwelling suffered water damage.

label: text
text: The appliances returned, to their Station 44 minutes after the receipt of the call.

label: paragraph_title
text: CANTON'S WAR FUNDS.

label: text
text: Canvassers are being sent out from Canton, states a report, to collect moneys from overseas Chinese, in aid of the Nationalist Government's expedition against the North.

label: paragraph_title
text: MONEY LOANS.

label: text
text: ASSOCIATION BOOKS ALLEGED

label: text
text: NAME ADDED?"

label: text
text: Fulfilcation of books was alleged in a case in the Summary Court this morning in which Wong Sham-chuen was sued by Chan Chung in respect of two Money Loan Associations of which it is alleged he is the head.

label: text
text: Plaintiff who was an undrawn member of these Associations, claimed return of subscriptions amounting to $100 in the first Money Loan Association and $150 in respect of the second. Breach of trust in failing to carry out duties as head of the Association is alleged.

label: text
text: Mr. U. McCallum appeared for the plaintiff and Mr. M. K. Lo defended.

label: text
text: Certain women who deposed "to being undrawn members of the Association were called by plaintiff as witnesses, stating either that they had been asked to join by the defendant himself or his deceased wife, Chan Ho. They looked on defendant as the head.

label: text
text: The defendant was called and denied directing the Association's. "Questioned us to his name appearing on certain books dealing with the affairs of the Association, defendant said that his wife had written his name.

label: text
text: Mr. Lo pointed out that the defendant's name was written in the books in different ink to the other entries. Asked by his Honour if he alleged falsification, Mr. Lo said that he did although he could enroll no evidence.

label: text
text:
His Honour examined the books and indicated that he was not in agreement with Mr. Lo.
His Honour also added that he would prefer hearing the evidence of drawn members of the Association as "such would not have a direct interest in the issue of this case and," he asked Mr. McCallum to endeavour to get into touch with drawn members.

label: text
text: The case was therefore adjourned as concerned the writ on the Money Lending Association issue. "With regard to a claim by the plaintiff for $81, money lent, His Honour gave judgment for plaintiff remarking that he believed plaintiff's evidence in preference to that of the defendant.

label: paragraph_title
text: GRAND PRIX.

label: text
text:
FIRST EVER HELD IN:
BRITAIN.
287 MILES MOTOR RACE.

label: text
text: The first "Grand Prize" motor race ever held in England took place yesterday at Brooklands over a course of 287 miles which was made to approximate as nearly as possible to road conditions by inclusion of sandbanks forming hairpin bends. There were eight corners to be taken in each circuit and 110 laps had to be covered.

label: text
text: R. E. Senischal, driving a Delage car, won the first prize. His average speed was 71.61 miles per hour.

label: text
text: Major Segrave, on a Talbot, made the fastest lap, covering 2.616 miles at a pace of 89.99 miles per hour.—British Wireless Service.

label: text
text: Britain Unplaced. An earlier Reuter states: —

label: text
text: The first motoring Grand Prix ever held in Britain, covering 110 laps, aggregating 287 miles, and in which there were 880 bends, was won by a Delage car, driven at first by Senechal and later by Wagner. It won by four laps, an average of 71.61 miles. Campbell, driving a Bugatti, was second, and another Delage third. Nine competed, five British and four French. The British were un-placed.

label: text
text: France having won the French-European-Grand Prix secures the world championship, the only other events concerned therein being the Indianapolis, five hundred miles, which was won by America, and the Italian Grand Prix, which is not yet decided.

label: paragraph_title
text: FALSE "ALARM.

label: text
text: FIRE ENGINE COLLIDES IN CITY.

label: text
text: FIREMAN INJURED

label: text
text:
Wiring Connections At Club
To Blame?

label: text
text:
Whilst proceeding to the Hong-
kong Club at 9.55 a.m. to-day in
response to an alarm which prov-
ed false, the No. 6 fire engine ap-
plince skidded on the damp road
surface and collided with a pillar
of the C.P.R. (Union) building at
the junction of Pedder Street and
Chatter Road.

label: text
text: Fireman No. 59 was jolted off the engine and sustained injuries to chest and neck which necessitated his removal to the Government Civil Hospital where he is progressing favourably.

label: text
text: The fire engine was damaged very considerably, the radiator being smashed in and the fire escape carried also being damaged. It was towed back to the station by another fire engine. It will be some time before the engine is again in commission but it is hoped to get the fire escape repaired and ready for use in the course of the day.

label: paragraph_title
text: Narrow Escape

label: text
text: Although the impact was considerable the pillar shows little signs of the collision. Needless to say, if the engine had not first struck the pillar and had entered through the C.P.R. window there might have been many more casualties as there were a number of people in the office at the time and the engine was travelling at considerable speed.

label: text
text: This is the second false fire alarm-within-two months from the Hongkong Club and is believed to have been due to defective wiring. The Club is connected up direct with the fire station and as soon as the indicator falls the brigade immediately gets busy. The falling of the signal does not; however, open up immediate telephonic communication with the Club and as seconds may be precious the fire station on both occasions has immediately sent the machines away without confirming an outbreak.

label: paragraph_title
text: Second False Alarm.

label: text
text: In June of this year a new alarm was put in at the Club and when the last false alarm occurred a glass cover which was being made for the push bell had not been completed. It was thought that the last alarm might have been due to this push bell having been accidentally touched. The push bell is now, however, under-glass-and-the-possibility-of-accidental contact is therefore removed. It is thought that a crossing of wires may have something to do with it and the Club authorities are having the connections examined.

label: text
text: ALLEGED YAUMATI ROBBERS CHARGED.

label: text
text: BROUGHT FROM MACAO.

label: text
text: Six men who are alleged to have taken part in an armed robbery at Woosung Street, Yaumati, on the morning of August 2, when booty of $1,500 consisting of cash and jewellery was taken away, were charged this morning before Mr. J. H. B. Nihill at the Kowloon Magistracy.

label: text
text:
It is alleged that the men were trying to make their “get away” in Macao when they were surprised by the local police there, who were notified of the fugitives’ arrival by the Hongkong police. After arrest, they were identified and brought back to Hongkong.
The case was formally remand-ed for a week.
